title: Countdown with stride
hints: `stride` can count down with a negative step.
`through:` includes the end value if you land on it; `to:` excludes it.
jsBridge: Swift dropped C-style `for (i = n; i >= 0; i -= s)` loops. `stride(from:through:by:)` (inclusive) and `stride(from:to:by:)` (exclusive) replace them and work with negative steps and floating-point values.

compass.q: `stride(from:to:)` vs `stride(from:through:)`: which includes the end? Which matches `..<` and which matches `...`?
Is there any loop in JS that Swift can't express without C-style `for`? Try a loop that modifies its own counter.
`stride(from: 0.0, through: 1.0, by: 0.1)`: does it include 1.0? Why is that shaky with floats?
Countdown timers in apps: is a loop right at all, or should you use `Timer`/`TimelineView`?
